# Why this run exists

`mean_loss` and `var_loss` are the two predictability nodes, and in the main
network they sit on an edge of about .70, by a wide margin the strongest in the
graph. A pair that tightly coupled can hold a community open between them, so
the placement of `mean_loss` alongside the dependency-MI indices might be
partly an artifact of having a near-duplicate node adjacent to it rather than a
statement about `mean_loss` itself.

This run drops `var_loss` and re-estimates everything. The question it answers
is narrow. Does `mean_loss` still land with `amod_mi`, `dobj_mi` and
`advmod_mi` when it has to get there without its twin?

Requested by Alex as a sensitivity check on the main analysis.

**How to read it.** Everything below is the main notebook's analysis run on 14
nodes instead of 15. Community *numbering* is arbitrary and will not match the
main notebook, so compare membership rather than labels. The companion run that
drops `mean_loss` instead is in `network-no-meanloss.qmd`.

```{r}
#| label: drop-parameter
#| code-fold: false

# The one predictability node held out of this run. Everything else is
# shared with the main notebook via ../_network-body.qmd.
drop_var <- "var_loss"
```
